items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: Lunsford, myself and a fellow, pianist, piano player by the name of Eddie Wilcox, we were in Lunsford's Ford.

ctx.x: -- the territory -- did you all work much?

Whenever we could get a job, and then when we got a job, Stanley, the booker would run off with the money. I remember one real rainy night in Cleveland the booker ran away with the money we were getting the money from a private gig that Jimmie Lunsford played in the band. He tore out in his car, raining like mad. And so Lunsford, myself and a fellow, pianist, piano player by the name of Eddie Wilcox, we were in Lunsford's Ford.

And we stayed right on his tail. And so we finally caught him, and so he said, well, here, man. Here's your money. Naturally, we wanted to jump on the guy, but we was too well bred for that, because he didn't know who you -- you know, what you were running into when you jumped down a man and jump on his back and try to do him in.
